name: Focus mode (AF-S / AF-C / AF-F / MF)

menu_path.z8: Photo shooting menu > Focus mode; or hold the focus-mode button and turn the main command dial
menu_path.z5ii: Photo shooting menu > Focus mode (also i menu)
menu_path.z50ii: Photo shooting menu > Focus mode (also i menu)

one_liner: Lock focus once (AF-S), keep tracking (AF-C), or focus by hand (MF).
what_it_does: Sets whether the camera focuses once and holds (AF-S), keeps re-focusing while you half-press or hold AF-ON (AF-C), or leaves focus to you (MF). AF-F is a video-only mode that focuses continuously without a button press. The default release behaviour differs: AF-S waits for focus, AF-C fires whether or not focus is achieved (changeable in a1/a2).

options.meaning: Single AF: focus locks on half-press; point turns green when locked, flashes red if it fails.
options.use_when: Static subjects: landscapes, tripod moonrise, posed portraits, static macro.

options.meaning: Continuous AF: focus keeps updating while the AF control is held.
options.use_when: Anything that moves: birds, dancers, running kids. Many shooters leave AF-C on full-time with back-button focus.

options.meaning: Camera switches between AF-S and AF-C depending on subject movement. Photo mode only.
options.use_when: Casual family snaps on the Z50II; avoid for serious action because you cannot predict which mode it picks.

options.meaning: Full-time AF, video mode only: focus adjusts continuously, locks on half-press.
options.use_when: Video when you want the camera to keep focusing without holding a button.

options.meaning: Manual focus; shutter fires regardless of focus. Peaking and the focus indicator can assist.
options.use_when: Stars, moon at long focal length, stacked macro, manual lenses (Thypoch, Laowa, Zeiss, Voigtlander, AF-D on FTZ II).

when_to_change: Switch to AF-C the moment the subject can move; switch to MF for night sky, high-magnification macro and manual lenses.

suggested.scenario: Stage dance in low LED light

suggested.value: AF-S (or MF after focusing with magnified view)
AF-C with a single point, or MF and rock the body; at 1:1 MF is usually more reliable
AF-S pinpoint/single on the moon's limb, then switch to MF so focus cannot shift

body_differences: Z8: AF-S, AF-C, AF-F (video), MF - no AF-A. Z50II: adds AF-A in photo mode. Z5II: Nikon's spec page does not list AF-A; confirm in camera.
gotchas: AF-S default is focus priority (shutter will not fire until focus is found); AF-C default is release priority - check a1/a2 if shots are blocked or soft.
With screw-drive AF/AF-D lenses on the FTZ II (e.g. 60mm f/2.8D, 105 DC, 50 f/1.8D) the body can only manual focus.
Z8 a9 Focus mode restrictions can hide modes from the button/dial cycle.
firmware_note: No functional change to the focus-mode list in Z8 FW 3.x, Z5II FW 1.20 or Z50II FW 1.10 found.
research_notes: Z5II AF-A availability not confirmed: the Z5II online manual body text could not be retrieved (only navigation), and the Nikon spec page does not mention AF-A.

name: AF-area mode

menu_path.z8: Photo shooting menu > AF-area mode; or hold the focus-mode button and turn the sub-command dial
menu_path.z5ii: Photo shooting menu > AF-area mode (also i menu)
menu_path.z50ii: Photo shooting menu > AF-area mode (also i menu)

one_liner: Decides which part of the frame the camera is allowed to focus on.
what_it_does: Controls how big the active focus area is and whether the camera or you choose where it sits. Small areas give precision on static subjects; larger or tracking areas keep moving subjects in focus. Subject detection only works in wide-area, 3D-tracking, subject-tracking and auto-area modes.

options.meaning: Very small point for precise focus; photo mode, AF-S only; slower.
options.use_when: Moon limb, eye of a static macro subject, focusing through foliage.

options.meaning: One user-selected point.
options.use_when: Static subjects where you choose exactly what is sharp; landscapes, tripod work.

options.meaning: Your chosen point, with surrounding points helping if the subject briefly slips off it. Photo mode, AF-C only. S is tightest.
options.use_when: Predictable movers you can keep under the point; bird on a branch with clutter; dancer's face when you want to stay on one performer.

options.meaning: Like single-point but a larger box; closest subject in the box gets priority. Subject detection works inside the box.
options.use_when: Subjects too fast for one point; panning; video. Good default for stage dance with People detection.

options.meaning: Custom-sized boxes you set by holding the OK button and resizing with the multi selector.
options.use_when: Birds in flight against sky (tall/wide box sized to the bird); a stage strip where dancers move side to side.

options.meaning: Start on the subject and the camera follows it across the frame while AF is held; reverts when released. Photo mode, AF-C only.
options.use_when: Erratic subjects: kids, BIF against clean backgrounds, a soloist moving across the stage.

options.meaning: Video-mode tracking of a selected subject; started with OK or half-press, ended with OK.
options.use_when: Video of a bird or dancer with the Z8 + 180-600.

options.meaning: Camera detects the subject and picks the point over the whole frame.
options.use_when: Kids, candid family shots, single bird against plain sky; least control when several subjects compete.

when_to_change: Go smaller when the camera grabs the wrong thing (branches, other dancers); go larger or tracking when you cannot keep a small point on the subject.

suggested.scenario: Stage dance in low LED light
suggested.value: Wide-area (S) + People detection; 3D-tracking for a soloist
Single-point (or Pinpoint) on the chosen focus distance
Single-point or Pinpoint; Dynamic (S) if the subject sways
Pinpoint or Single-point on the moon's edge, AF-S

body_differences: Nikon's spec pages list the same set on all three bodies: Pinpoint (photo), Single, Dynamic S/M/L (photo), Wide S/L/C1/C2, Auto-area, 3D-tracking (photo), Subject-tracking (video). Z8 FW 3.00 added more custom wide-area (C1/C2) size patterns. Z5II and Z50II use the same Expeed 7 subject detection family, but the Z8's stacked sensor gives faster AF updates during bursts.
gotchas: Pinpoint only in AF-S; Dynamic and 3D only in AF-C - the menu greys them out otherwise.
Subject detection is ignored in Single-point, Pinpoint and Dynamic modes.
3D-tracking resets to the start point when you release AF; recompose before re-engaging.
Tracking can fail on subjects with the same colour/brightness as the background, very small or fast subjects, or when obstructed.
firmware_note: Z8 FW 3.00: wider/more custom wide-area AF focus-area patterns (Nikon download center change log).
research_notes: Z8 and Z5II option descriptions are taken from Nikon spec pages plus the Z50II manual text; the Z8/Z5II online manual bodies could not be retrieved, only their menu indexes.

one_liner: Tells the AF what kind of subject to look for: people, animals, birds, vehicles.
what_it_does: Points the deep-learning detector at a subject class so the camera can find faces/eyes/heads or vehicles inside the active AF area. Detection works in Wide-area, 3D-tracking, Subject-tracking and Auto-area. Narrowing the class (e.g. Birds instead of Auto) reduces false grabs on other subject types.

options.meaning: Looks for people, animals and vehicles and picks one.
options.use_when: Mixed scenes; family outings where kids and dogs share the frame.

options.meaning: Faces and eyes (and bodies).
options.use_when: Kids, portraits, stage dance.

options.meaning: Dogs, cats and birds (face/eye or whole animal).
options.use_when: Mammals and mixed wildlife.

options.meaning: Bird heads/eyes or whole bird.
options.use_when: Birding with the 180-600; more decisive than Animal on small birds.

options.meaning: Cars, motorbikes, trains, bicycles (and aircraft on bodies without a separate option).
options.use_when: Motorsport, trains.

options.meaning: Aircraft body, nose or cockpit.
options.use_when: Airshows.

options.meaning: No detection; pure area-based AF.
options.use_when: Landscapes, macro, moon - where detection would only add false hits.

when_to_change: Change whenever your subject class changes; turn it off for static non-living subjects.

suggested.scenario: Stage dance in low LED light

suggested.value: People (Auto if the dog joins in)
Off (Animal can sometimes find insect eyes, but is unreliable)

body_differences: Z8: Birds option added in FW 2.00; FW 3.00 added subject-detection priority for MF and MF detection areas. Z5II: Nikon lists nine detectable subjects (people, birds, dogs, cats, cars, bicycles, motorcycles, trains, airplanes). Z50II manual lists Auto, People, Animal, Birds, Vehicle, Airplanes, Off.
gotchas: Detection performance drops in high-speed frame capture+ and with HLG tone mode (Z50II manual).
Under fluorescent/mercury lights Birds detection can be affected by flicker - Photo flicker reduction may help.
Turn the AF-assist illuminator off for animals - it can affect their eyes.
When several subjects are detected, grey boxes appear; move between them with the multi selector left/right.
firmware_note: Z8: Birds in FW 2.00; MF subject detection in FW 3.00. Z5II/Z50II: no detection changes in FW 1.20/1.10 change logs.

name: a1 AF-C priority selection

one_liner: In AF-C, fire immediately (Release) or only when in focus (Focus).
what_it_does: Only applies in AF-C. Release lets the shutter fire on every press regardless of focus; Focus blocks the shot until the camera thinks it is in focus; Focus + release gives focus priority to the first frame of a burst on dark or low-contrast subjects and release priority after that.

options.meaning: Shutter always fires; burst rate never slows for focus.
options.use_when: Action where timing matters more than every frame being sharp (Nikon's recommendation for all sports in its Sports AF guide).

options.meaning: First frame of a burst waits for focus in dim/low-contrast light; later frames release.
options.use_when: Stage dance and dim indoor kids - protects the first frame without stalling the burst.

options.meaning: Shutter only fires when focus is achieved.
options.use_when: When a missed-focus frame is worse than a missed moment; rarely ideal for fast action.

when_to_change: Use Release for bright, fast action; switch to Focus + release when light is poor and the first frame keeps missing.

suggested.scenario: Stage dance in low LED light

suggested.value: Release (you time the shot as you rock into focus)

body_differences: Same three options on all three bodies (verified in the Z50II manual; present as a1 on Z8 and Z5II menu indexes).
gotchas: Has no effect in AF-S - use a2 for that.
Release priority means the camera will happily record out-of-focus frames; it does not make AF faster.
research_notes: Option labels confirmed from Z50II manual; Z8/Z5II confirmed present at a1 via menu index only.

when_to_change: Raise it if AF keeps jumping to foreground clutter; lower it if AF is slow to pick up a new subject you deliberately switched to.

one_liner: Choose whether half-pressing the shutter focuses, or only AF-ON does.
what_it_does: Shutter/AF-ON lets both the shutter half-press and AF-ON focus. AF-ON only removes focusing from the shutter button (back-button focus), so you can lock focus by releasing AF-ON and fire freely. A sub-option, Out-of-focus release, decides whether the shutter can fire when not in focus in AF-ON-only mode.

options.meaning: Half-press focuses; AF-ON also focuses.
options.use_when: Simple handling; lending the camera to family.

options.meaning: Only the AF-ON (or an assigned button) focuses.

options.meaning: Shutter fires even if not in focus.
options.use_when: Most BBF users - you decide when focus is good.

options.meaning: Shutter fires only when in focus.
options.use_when: Rarely; can block shots in dim light.

when_to_change: Set once; BBF pays off for birds, dance and kids. Revert to Shutter/AF-ON before handing the camera to someone else.

suggested.scenario: Stage dance in low LED light

AF-ON only or Shutter/AF-ON - personal preference
AF-ON only (focus once, then shoot without refocusing)

gotchas: With AF-ON only, Out-of-focus release Disable and Pinpoint AF, the shutter can still release regardless of focus (Z50II manual note).

options.meaning: Higher shows more depth as 'in focus'.
options.use_when: Use 1 for critical focus (macro, stars); 2 general; 3 for quick zone focus.

one_liner: Brightens the viewfinder in darkness and extends AF to lower light.
what_it_does: Brightens the live view so you can compose in very dark scenes, and Nikon's manuals say it improves focusing in low light (photo mode only). Nikon rates AF detection to -9 EV with starlight view on the Z8 (-7 EV without). The display may become slightly jerky and the histogram is hidden.

options.meaning: Brighter, slower-refresh display; extended low-light AF in photo mode.
options.use_when: Night sky, moonrise in twilight, very dark interiors with static subjects.

options.meaning: Normal display refresh.
options.use_when: Any action - the laggy display hurts tracking.

when_to_change: Turn on for night/astro composition and static low-light AF; off for moving subjects.

suggested.scenario: Stage dance in low LED light
suggested.value: OFF (display lag; stage is usually brighter than starlight-view territory)
ON while composing the dim foreground; AF on the moon itself does not need it

body_differences: Z8: -7 to +19 EV, -9 EV with starlight view (Nikon spec). Z5II: Nikon quotes -10 EV (spec doesn't state whether starlight view is required). Z50II: -9 to +19 EV in spec. Z8 FW 3.00 adds a14 Maximum aperture Lv, which focuses at maximum aperture in live view and can also help in dim light.
gotchas: Histogram disappears while it is on.
Photo mode only - does nothing for video AF.
EV figures are for f/1.2 lenses at ISO 100 in AF-S, centre point; slower zooms like the 180-600 lose that margin.

one_liner: Shows face/eye boxes while you focus manually, to guide manual lenses.
what_it_does: In MF, the camera still runs subject detection and draws boxes on detected subjects, and the in-focus indicator can then judge focus on that subject. All searches the whole frame; Wide (L)/(S) limit detection to the current focus area; Off disables it. The subject class comes from AF/MF subject detection options.

options.meaning: Detect anywhere; grey boxes on extra subjects, switch with left/right.
options.use_when: Portraits with a manual lens where the subject moves around the frame.

options.meaning: Detect only inside the focus area.
options.use_when: Several people in frame and you want a specific one.

options.meaning: No detection in MF.

when_to_change: Turn on when shooting people with the Thypoch 28, Voigtlander 58 or Zeiss 35; off for everything non-living.

suggested.value: Wide (S) if using a manual lens - otherwise n/a
All, if using a manual lens

name: a16 Focus limiter setting

one_liner: In-body near/far focus range so AF can't hunt to infinity or the foreground.
what_it_does: Lets you set a minimum and maximum focus distance in-camera so the AF only searches within that band. Nikon pitches it for reducing hunting, helping in low light and with fast subjects, and keeping AF off the background. Works independently of any lens limiter switch.

options.meaning: AF restricted to the stored distance range.
options.use_when: Birds over water or against distant backgrounds; a stage at a fixed distance from your seat.

when_to_change: Set when AF keeps jumping to the background or hunting through the full range on a long lens.

suggested.value: Limit to the realistic flight distance band (e.g. 6 m to infinity at a feeder; tighter over open water)

suggested.scenario: Stage dance in low LED light
suggested.value: Limit to roughly stage-front to back wall from your seat
Optional: limit to close range to stop hunting to infinity

body_differences: Z8 only (FW 3.00+). Not in the Z5II or Z50II Custom Settings menus.
gotchas: Forgetting it is on makes AF refuse subjects outside the range - add it to My Menu or a button to see it.
